item.title: Managing cropland edges as multifunctional interfaces for sustainable agriculture
item.content:encoded:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00844-5

Cropland edges are commonly treated as unproductive remnants or generic conservation strips, yet they constitute dynamic and selectively permeable interfaces between cropped fields and surrounding land. Managing complementary edge portfolios, rather than maximizing edge area or prescribing uniform widths, could reconcile production, biodiversity and climate resilience while limiting cross-boundary risks.

item.title: The Arctic carbon cycle response to changing root and rhizosphere processes amid greening and permafrost thaw
item.content:encoded:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00832-9

Arctic warming is rapidly transforming belowground processes and carbon cycling. In this Review, the authors synthesize how root and rhizosphere processes shape carbon balance under permafrost thaw and vegetation change and propose integrative approaches to improve mechanistic understanding and model representation.
